chunks: And it is reported from Nadir the servant who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), whenever one of us was eating, would not get him to attend to something until he was free from his meal.

key_terms.يَسْتَخْدِمُهُ: He would employ/use him (for a task)

ai.seo_question: What was the etiquette of Imam Al-Reza (AS) towards his servants during meal times?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of *adab* (etiquette) within the Imamate, where Imam al-Rida (AS) demonstrated profound respect for the natural rhythm of his servant's daily needs. It underscores the Shia principle that spiritual authority is accompanied by humane consideration, ensuring that servants are not interrupted during essential acts like eating, thereby fostering a relationship of dignity rather than mere servitude. This specific behavior reflects the broader prophetic tradition of attending to the physical well-being of others as an act of worship.
